frozen: 2026-11-24, before R2-R5 were built (R1 = the harness baseline)

requirements.name: Drag the time on any figure, everything follows
requirements.why: Zach named it as the important thing: dragging time on any figure syncs across all the others. It is the viewer's core loop.
requirements.passCondition: A drag on any chart commits the time live; every shown chart (and another tab when opened), the 3D pose and the slider read back within one sample; discoverable without instructions.

anchors.1: Only one slider commits time; charts preview at best.
anchors.3: Charts commit time, but only some figures follow, or not live, or it needs a mode or a hidden gesture.
anchors.5: Any figure, live while dragging, every figure + 3D + slider within one sample, in every tab, with an obvious affordance.

requirements.name: Compare 2 to 40 runs and keep it legible
requirements.why: The dataset viewer will import this viewer and hand it a bunch of runs (keep=); the bam_fb target alone has 17 lines in 8 configs.
requirements.passCondition: keep= honoured; toggling a run is one click and updates every figure; at 17 runs the first chart is visible without scrolling past controls and colours stay readable.

anchors.1: Runs beyond a handful bury the charts or collide visually; toggling is hard to find.
anchors.3: Works at 17 runs but the controls or legend eat the first screen, or repeats pile into spaghetti.
anchors.5: 17 runs read as clearly as 3: grouped, toggled in one click, charts on the first screen, repeats summarised when many.

requirements.name: Get to the moment that matters
requirements.why: The first question on the page is 'when was it worst?'; finding and reading that instant across runs is the review's payoff.
requirements.passCondition: The worst moment (and other notable moments) is reachable in one action and the value of every shown run at the playhead is readable.

anchors.1: The reader hunts for the moment by eye and reads values by hovering one chart at a time.
anchors.3: A jump to the worst moment exists; values at the playhead need hovering.
anchors.5: Moments are listed or marked and jumped to in one action; every run's value at the playhead is shown.

requirements.name: Same thing as Rerun, and a way back
requirements.why: HTML and Rerun are peers ('either our custom one or the rerun one'); the target view is where the reader came from.
requirements.passCondition: Open the same in Rerun carries the shown runs, the open tab and the time; the back link returns to the target view with the selection; tab names and layout match Rerun's.

anchors.1: No way across; different names or layout from Rerun.
anchors.3: Both links work; the layouts differ enough that switching needs re-orientation.
anchors.5: Both links carry selection (and time/tab for Rerun); the HTML and Rerun read as the same viewer.

requirements.name: Keeps the frozen structure and Zach's UI rules
requirements.why: NAVIGATION.md Part B is frozen (stage + question tabs, same in Rerun); his standing UI rules apply to every surface.
requirements.passCondition: Stage beside the question tabs with exact titles; titles name signal/joint/sign/unit; degrees; joints one per row; boundaries drag and are remembered; panels fold; plain words; no silent truncation.

anchors.1: Breaks the frozen structure or several rules.
anchors.3: Keeps the structure; one or two rules slip (a fixed boundary, a cryptic label, a clipped name).
anchors.5: Structure intact and every rule visibly kept.

requirements.name: Cheap and safe to splice into traj_compare
requirements.why: The pick gets spliced into production plots.js, which the dataset viewer, TTA and the bench all render with.
requirements.passCondition: The change to plots.js / viewer3d.js / style.css is small, local and needs no contract change.

anchors.1: A rewrite of the page assembly or a new contract.
anchors.3: A few hundred lines touching layout and the chart builder; a contract addition.
anchors.5: A contained addition (gesture + playhead) on today's assembly; no contract change.

hardGates.name: Real data only
hardGates.why: Both fixtures are real runs (TTA's workspace-dev-000; the bench's BAM FB target); nothing synthetic.

hardGates.name: Drag-to-sync proven on both fixtures
hardGates.why: check.json: mid-drag, after release and on another tab, every shown chart + slider + 3D within one sample.

hardGates.name: x zoom still works
hardGates.why: check.json: the variant's zoom gesture narrows every chart alike and resets.

hardGates.name: keep= honoured and a toggle updates every figure
hardGates.why: check.json: shown = keep; a toggled-off run leaves every chart and the 3D.

hardGates.name: Back to the target view and Open the same in Rerun
hardGates.why: check.json: back href carries keep=; the recording holds exactly the shown runs at the playhead time.

hardGates.name: Production untouched
hardGates.why: No edit under src/traj_compare; each variant carries its own copies.
